raw: {"analysis":"Response QTD provides a more operationally sound plan, correctly addressing the 30-second lock constraint with batched backfill logic (under 1000 rows/transaction with explicit sleeps), while Response ZWR dangerously suggests executing the full migration within the 30-second window. QTD also better manages CI costs by recommending sampled subsets for intermediate lanes and reserving the full 2TB run for the final candidate, whereas ZWR doesn't address the $120/run cost constraint. Both plans correctly identify the critical path around the daily-reconciliation shared library and the need for dual approval from the Lead Architect and Data Governance Officer.","verdict":"QTD"}
